summary:
I built and ran a standalone C++20 prototype of the synthetic content for §3.2's two acceptance tests (D-069). It uses libavformat, libavcodec, libavutil and libswscale only; the ffmpeg and ffprobe binaries were never run. It writes two local HLS ladders. Each has three rungs (640x360, 480x270, 320x180), 8 segments of 1 s at 25 fps (200 frames) in MPEG-TS, a master playlist whose BANDWIDTH values are measured from the segments, and a ground-truth layout.json.

- **Degraded-segment ladder:** segment 4 of v270 is encoded at QP 46, every other segment at QP 22.
- **Ad-boundary ladder:** main content in segments 0-2 and 5-7. The ad is in segments 3-4, between EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY tags, with EXT-X-CUE-OUT:2.000 before it, CUE-OUT-CONT before its second segment and CUE-IN after it. v180's ad is encoded at QP 46.

I scored both with the Phase 2 mirage_vmaf (SHA-256 454db2ed…435b), mostly in top-rung mode and once against a lossless FFV1 mezzanine. tables.py recomputes the per-segment mean and minimum VMAF from the reports.

- **Degraded ladder:** the drop is clear and confined exactly to segment 4's frames 100-124. The ad ladder's drop is confined exactly to the ad's frames 75-124. The control rung of each ladder has no drop.
- **Encoders and determinism:** the same holds with FFmpeg's native MPEG-2 encoder. Each ladder was generated twice and all 29 files matched by SHA-256; an unoptimized build of the generator gave the same files.
- **Times:** generating a ladder takes about 2 s, scoring it about 0.5 s. An unoptimized build (as the Debug tests are compiled) needs 16.9 s to generate.

The other variants each show one problem, detailed in testgen.md. They are:
- the existing ramp as the source;
- a busy versus a calm ad, each with a normal-quantizer control;
- the ad's timestamps starting at 10 s, 1 s and 0 s;
- continuity counters with and without the TS discontinuity indicator;
- a one-file mezzanine for the ad ladder.

Every run's command and full stdout/stderr are saved under testgen/logs by run_all.sh, with local paths replaced by placeholders. testgen.md cites a log for each number, lists the owner's design choices with the agent's recommendations, and notes where nothing was measured (MEASUREMENT PENDING). Nothing was written outside the output directory, and no state-changing git command was run.
files: <out>/testgen/logs/ (81 records of the final pass: command, cwd, full stdout/stderr, exit status, wall time)
<out>/testgen/reports/ (14 mirage_vmaf reports, release and debug, with each ladder's layout.json; relative paths only)
<out>/testgen/media/ (generated ladders and FFV1 mezzanines; regenerable, not for committing)
<out>/testgen/ffmpeg-n8.1.1/ (FFmpeg n8.1.1 source files fetched from GitHub for reading)
key_findings: Degraded-segment content works (libx264). v270 segment 4 at QP 46 has a mean VMAF of 41.239, against 97.134-98.231 in its other segments. The frames more than 6 points below the pair's median are exactly frames 100-124, segment 4's 25 frames. In the control rung v180 only frame 0 is. A trailing-median prototype detector finds one drop, frames 100-124. Evidence: testgen/logs/15_degraded_x264_tables.txt. MPEG-2 gives segment 4 a mean of 62.022 against 96.923-97.671 (logs/25). Mezzanine mode gives the same drop, while v360 scores 100.000 in segments 1-7 (logs/18).

Ad-boundary content works (libx264, calm ad). v180's ad segments score 27.409 and 27.380 against 90.966-91.978 for the main content. The low frames are exactly 75-124, from the segment after EXT-X-CUE-OUT through the one before EXT-X-CUE-IN. The control rung v270, whose ad is at QP 22, has a single low frame, the ad's first (logs/46). With v180's ad at QP 22 its ad segments score 90.599 and 90.027 (logs/49). The 'busy' ad at QP 22 scores 84.814 and 85.635, with 27 frames past the threshold (logs/59c), so the calm ad is the default.

The existing tests' ramp is a poor source. Its measured BANDWIDTH for v270 (234624) is higher than for v360 (169952), so the ladder is refused and the top-rung rule would pick v270 (logs/30, logs/31). The noise source's top rung takes 596336 bytes against the ramp's 163184 at the same QP (logs/10, logs/31).

Determinism: all four ladders, generated twice, give 29 of 29 files with the same SHA-256 (logs/12, 22, 42, 52), and an -O0 build of the generator against the -O2 build gives the same (logs/91). x264 is core 165 r3222 b35605a (logs/10), the commit the Docker image pins (repo docker/Dockerfile:60, docker/README.md:37). The debug-build mirage_vmaf reproduces the release program's scores (logs/99a, 99b).

Wall times on a shared Apple M3 Pro (logs/05): generation takes 2.022-2.313 s and scoring 0.457-0.515 s per ladder (logs/10, 20, 40, 50, 14, 24, 45, 54). Generation at -O0, as the debug preset compiles tests (-g with no -O, repo build/macos-debug/build.ninja:1229), takes 16.941 s (logs/90).

FFmpeg 8.1.1's hls demuxer ignores EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY. Its parser handles only STREAM-INF through BYTERANGE (libavformat/hls.c:861-980), and it reads all segments as one stream through one sub-demuxer (hls.c:1641-1754, 2271-2272, 2371). Timestamps therefore jump as written: -2.96 s before frame 75 and +3.04 s before frame 125, in v180 and in the reference v360 alike (logs/43, logs/44).

Continuity counters that restart unmarked after EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY are allowed by RFC 8216 §3 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8216#section-3). FFmpeg then marks the packets corrupt (libavformat/mpegts.c:3012-3034, demux.c:587-595). The probe shows 8 continuity failures and 2 packets flagged corrupt, landing one frame early (logs/61), and mirage_vmaf prints 16 stderr warnings (logs/65). The scores are unchanged (logs/64), and the report records none of the warnings.

mirage_vmaf's discontinuity sequences are not the playlist's. With the ad's PTS starting at 10 s, the +3.04 s forward jump does not count as a discontinuity (logs/01 --help: back, or forward by more than 10 s). Each input then has 2 sequences, {0,10,75} and {75,10,125}, where the playlist has three; all 200 frames still pair under D-046/D-050 (logs/46). With the ad starting at 1 s each input has 3 sequences (logs/73).

PTS repeat across the splice: frames 0 and 75 both have ref_pts 10 (logs/46b). A §3.1 timeline keyed by media PTS alone cannot place them; ref_index (the frame's position), or the discontinuity sequence together with the PTS, can.

A sequence whose first DTS would be negative is silently shifted. With the ad's PTS starting at 0 and libx264's B-frame delay, the ad's first frame lands at 0.080 s (logs/75), from the muxer's avoid_negative_ts (libavformat/mux.c:413-419).

Mezzanine mode cannot score the ad ladder against a one-file mezzanine whose timestamps continue through the ad. D-050 stops the pairing at the rungs' first jump: 75 frames paired, 250 failed (76.92%), and the exit status is still 0 with D-028's warning (logs/81, logs/82).

The existing tests' MPEG-2 helpers set global_quality, which FFmpeg 8.1.1's MPEG-2 encoder doesn't read; it takes the quantizer from each frame's quality (mpegvideo_enc.c:3618-3652). Their qscale is therefore the qmin clip of 2 (mpegvideo_enc.c:215-217, options_table.h:105), which matches their intended 2 by coincidence (repo tests/test_vmaf_ladder.cpp:126). This comes from reading the source, not from a run.

SCTE-35 DATERANGE and OATCLS forms are left out of the ladders. The only citable splice_info_sections don't fit a 2 s ad: RFC 8216 §8.10 has a 59.993 s break, and AWS's OATCLS example goes with CUE-OUT:201.467. The cue syntax follows the AWS MediaLive 'Elemental' form (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/medialive/latest/ug/sample-manifests-hls.html), placed as in MediaTailor's origin example. MediaTailor's stitched playlists drop the cue tags and keep only DISCONTINUITY (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediatailor/latest/ug/manifest-hls-example.html).
open_issues: Whether another machine, Linux/x86 or the Docker image, writes the same bytes is MEASUREMENT PENDING; only one machine was used. The mezzanines' determinism was not compared.

The work order's example of a 2.3 s segment request needs network timing. tests/HttpFileServer.h can hold or cut a response but not delay one (tests/HttpFileServer.h:32-36), so a delay rule would be needed; not prototyped.
For the owner: how the §3.1 timeline keys frames, given the PTS collision. Options: (discontinuity sequence, PTS), position, or playlist time.
For the owner: where the timeline takes discontinuity sequences from. The report's sequences differ from the playlist's.
For the owner: whether a bare EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY, as in MediaTailor-style stitched playlists without cue tags, counts as an ad boundary.
Owner decisions with the agent's recommendations in testgen.md §4. Encoder: libx264, skipping the test when absent, or mpeg2video.
Owner decisions (testgen.md §4): calm or busy ad content.
Owner decisions (testgen.md §4): the ad's PTS origin (10 s, which collides with the main content, or 1 s).
Owner decisions (testgen.md §4): whether continuity counters are marked at the splice.
Owner decisions (testgen.md §4): SCTE-35 binary forms. Recommended: leave them out of the ladders and use RFC 8216 §8.10 as decoder test vectors.
Owner decisions (testgen.md §4): the detection window and N. Single-frame dips at the start of each libvmaf context must be ignored.
Owner decisions (testgen.md §4): mezzanine mode in the tests.
Generation in a Debug build takes 16.941 s per ladder. Options: compile the generator source optimized, a faster noise, smaller frames, or one fixture per run. Their effect is MEASUREMENT PENDING.
If §3.1's decoder events are to include FFmpeg's corrupt-packet warnings, the analyzer must capture av_log messages or packet flags; the report has neither today.
Not generated: an ad that is low quality in every rung including the top rung. That case hides the drop in top-rung mode (D-002's limit).
Only the prototype's binary forms, the DATERANGE and OATCLS SCTE-35 forms, were left out; the plain CUE-OUT, CUE-OUT-CONT and CUE-IN tags are present.
testgen/ffmpeg-n8.1.1/ and refs/ are copies made for reading and are better cited by URL than committed. testgen/media/ is large and regenerable.
In testgen/explore/, the first failed MPEG-2 generation's log was overwritten by its rerun under the same name.
